question: She is thought ___ the country last week.
fr: On pense qu'elle a quitté le pays la semaine dernière.

explain.fr: Passif « reporting » + to have + participe (antériorité).
explain.en: Reporting passive + to have + participle (earlier action).

say: She is thought to have left the country last week.

question: He was made ___ for the damage.
fr: On l'a obligé à payer les dégâts.

explain.fr: make au passif : be made + to + verbe.
explain.en: “Make” in the passive: be made + to + verb.

say: He was made to pay for the damage.

question: There's no point ___ about it now.
fr: Ça ne sert à rien de s'en inquiéter maintenant.

explain.fr: There's no point in + -ing.
explain.en: There's no point in + -ing.

say: There's no point in worrying about it now.

question: I can't help ___ that something is wrong.
fr: Je ne peux m'empêcher de sentir que quelque chose ne va pas.

explain.fr: can't help + -ing = ne pas pouvoir s'empêcher de.
explain.en: can't help + -ing.

say: I can't help feeling that something is wrong.

question: She went on ___ even though nobody was listening.
fr: Elle a continué à parler même si personne n'écoutait.

explain.fr: go on + -ing = continuer la même action.
explain.en: go on + -ing = continue the same action.

say: She went on talking even though nobody was listening.

question: After the introduction, he went on ___ the results.
fr: Après l'introduction, il est passé à la présentation des résultats.

explain.fr: go on + to = passer à une nouvelle action.
explain.en: go on + to = move on to a new action.

say: After the introduction, he went on to present the results.

question: I mean ___ the report by Friday.
fr: J'ai l'intention de finir le rapport d'ici vendredi.

explain.fr: mean + to = avoir l'intention de.
explain.en: mean + to = intend to.

say: I mean to finish the report by Friday.

question: Taking the job would mean ___ to another city.
fr: Accepter le poste impliquerait de déménager dans une autre ville.

explain.fr: mean + -ing = impliquer.
explain.en: mean + -ing = involve.

say: Taking the job would mean moving to another city.

question: You ___ have warned me! I could have avoided the accident.
fr: Tu aurais pu me prévenir ! J'aurais pu éviter l'accident.

explain.fr: Reproche : might / could have + participe.
explain.en: Reproach: might / could have + participle.

say: You might have warned me! I could have avoided the accident.

question: She ___ well be right, but I still disagree.
fr: Elle a peut-être bien raison, mais je ne suis toujours pas d'accord.

explain.fr: may well = il est bien possible que.
explain.en: may well = it is quite possible that.

say: She may well be right, but I still disagree.

question: I ___ as well stay at home; it's too late to go out.
fr: Autant rester à la maison ; il est trop tard pour sortir.

explain.fr: might as well = autant (faute de mieux).
explain.en: might as well = there's no better option.

say: I might as well stay at home; it's too late to go out.

question: He ___ have been more than twenty when he became famous.
fr: Il ne pouvait pas avoir plus de vingt ans quand il est devenu célèbre.

explain.fr: Impossibilité dans le passé : can't have + participe.
explain.en: Past impossibility: can't have + participle.

say: He can't have been more than twenty when he became famous.

question: You ___ to have handed in your essay yesterday.
fr: Tu étais censé rendre ta dissertation hier.

explain.fr: be supposed to = être censé (attente non remplie).
explain.en: be supposed to (unfulfilled expectation).

say: You were supposed to have handed in your essay yesterday.

question: The matter ___ at the next meeting.
fr: La question doit être abordée à la prochaine réunion.

explain.fr: be to + be + participe : arrangement officiel.
explain.en: be to + be + participle: official arrangement.

say: The matter is to be discussed at the next meeting.

question: It ___ that the economy will recover next year.
fr: On s'attend à ce que l'économie se redresse l'année prochaine.

explain.fr: It is expected / said / believed that… (passif impersonnel).
explain.en: It is expected / said / believed that… (impersonal passive).

say: It is expected that the economy will recover next year.

question: The new law ___ into force next month.
fr: La nouvelle loi doit entrer en vigueur le mois prochain.

explain.fr: be due to + verbe = être prévu pour.
explain.en: be due to + verb = be scheduled to.

say: The new law is due to come into force next month.

question: She hates ___ in public.
fr: Elle déteste être critiquée en public.

explain.fr: Gérondif passif.
explain.en: Passive gerund.

say: She hates being criticized in public.

question: ___ of the two proposals was accepted.
fr: Aucune des deux propositions n'a été acceptée.

explain.fr: Pour deux éléments : neither of + verbe au singulier.
explain.en: For two items: neither of + singular verb.

say: Neither of the two proposals was accepted.

question: You can take ___ road; they both lead to the village.
fr: Tu peux prendre l'une ou l'autre route ; elles mènent toutes les deux au village.

explain.fr: either + nom singulier = l'un ou l'autre.
explain.en: either + singular noun = one or the other.

say: You can take either road; they both lead to the village.

question: A number of students ___ complained.
fr: Un certain nombre d'étudiants se sont plaints.

explain.fr: A number of + pluriel → verbe pluriel ; « The number of » → singulier.
explain.en: A number of + plural → plural verb; “The number of” → singular.

say: A number of students have complained.

question: The number of applicants ___ risen sharply.
fr: Le nombre de candidats a fortement augmenté.

explain.fr: The number of… → verbe au singulier.
explain.en: The number of… → singular verb.

say: The number of applicants has risen sharply.

question: Ten kilometers ___ a long way to walk.
fr: Dix kilomètres, c'est long à pied.

explain.fr: Quantité vue comme un tout : verbe au singulier.
explain.en: Quantity seen as a whole: singular verb.

say: Ten kilometers is a long way to walk.

question: The candidates, none of ___ had any experience, were rejected.
fr: Les candidats, dont aucun n'avait d'expérience, ont été refusés.

explain.fr: Quantifieur + of whom.
explain.en: Quantifier + of whom.

say: The candidates, none of whom had any experience, were rejected.

question: This is the house in ___ Shakespeare was born.
fr: Voici la maison dans laquelle Shakespeare est né.

explain.fr: Préposition + which (that impossible après une préposition).
explain.en: Preposition + which (“that” is impossible after a preposition).

say: This is the house in which Shakespeare was born.

question: He gave me a book, the title of ___ I've forgotten.
fr: Il m'a donné un livre dont j'ai oublié le titre.

explain.fr: the + nom + of which (soutenu) = dont.
explain.en: the + noun + of which (formal).

say: He gave me a book, the title of which I've forgotten.

question: Anyone ___ wishes to attend should register online.
fr: Toute personne souhaitant y assister doit s'inscrire en ligne.

explain.fr: Anyone who…
explain.en: Anyone who…

say: Anyone who wishes to attend should register online.

question: ___ the bad weather, the event went ahead.
fr: Malgré le mauvais temps, l'événement a eu lieu.

explain.fr: notwithstanding + nom (très soutenu) = malgré.
explain.en: notwithstanding + noun (very formal) = despite.

say: Notwithstanding the bad weather, the event went ahead.

question: He's very talented; ___, he lacks discipline.
fr: Il est très doué ; il manque néanmoins de discipline.

explain.fr: nonetheless / nevertheless = néanmoins.
explain.en: nonetheless / nevertheless.

say: He's very talented; nonetheless, he lacks discipline.

question: The plan was successful, ___ only partially.
fr: Le plan a réussi, bien que partiellement.

explain.fr: albeit + adjectif / adverbe = bien que.
explain.en: albeit + adjective / adverb = although.

say: The plan was successful, albeit only partially.

question: ___ as I admire him, I can't support this decision.
fr: J'ai beau l'admirer, je ne peux pas soutenir cette décision.

explain.fr: Much as + proposition = bien que, avoir beau.
explain.en: Much as + clause = although.

say: Much as I admire him, I can't support this decision.

question: ___ we like it or not, prices will rise.
fr: Que cela nous plaise ou non, les prix vont augmenter.

explain.fr: Whether… or not = que… ou non.
explain.en: Whether… or not.

say: Whether we like it or not, prices will rise.

question: ___ the circumstances, we did quite well.
fr: Vu les circonstances, nous nous en sommes plutôt bien sortis.

explain.fr: Given + nom = vu, étant donné.
explain.en: Given + noun = considering.

say: Given the circumstances, we did quite well.

question: He resigned, ___ allowing a younger colleague to take over.
fr: Il a démissionné, permettant ainsi à un collègue plus jeune de prendre la relève.

explain.fr: thereby + -ing = ce faisant, de ce fait.
explain.en: thereby + -ing = as a result of this.

say: He resigned, thereby allowing a younger colleague to take over.

question: They signed an agreement ___ both companies share the profits.
fr: Ils ont signé un accord en vertu duquel les deux entreprises partagent les bénéfices.

explain.fr: whereby = en vertu duquel / par lequel.
explain.en: whereby = by which.

say: They signed an agreement whereby both companies share the profits.

question: By next spring, she ___ at the company for twenty years.
fr: Au printemps prochain, cela fera vingt ans qu'elle travaille dans l'entreprise.

explain.fr: Durée jusqu'à un point futur : future perfect continu.
explain.en: Duration up to a future point: future perfect continuous.

say: By next spring, she will have been working at the company for twenty years.

question: I ___ about changing jobs for a while now.
fr: Ça fait un moment que je pense à changer de travail.

explain.fr: Activité qui dure jusqu'à maintenant : present perfect continu.
explain.en: Activity continuing up to now: present perfect continuous.

say: I have been thinking about changing jobs for a while now.

question: She ___ the house when the storm broke.
fr: Elle était sur le point de quitter la maison quand l'orage a éclaté.

explain.fr: be about to + verbe = être sur le point de.
explain.en: be about to + verb.

say: She was about to leave the house when the storm broke.

question: The President ___ the country next week.
fr: Le président doit se rendre dans le pays la semaine prochaine.

explain.fr: be to + verbe : projet officiel (presse).
explain.en: be to + verb: official plan (newspapers).

say: The President is to visit the country next week.

question: This is the third time you ___ late this week.
fr: C'est la troisième fois que tu es en retard cette semaine.

explain.fr: This is the first / second… time + present perfect.
explain.en: This is the first / second… time + present perfect.

say: This is the third time you have been late this week.

question: The more I read, the ___ I understand.
fr: Plus je lis, moins je comprends.

explain.fr: the more…, the less…
explain.en: the more…, the less…

say: The more I read, the less I understand.

question: The hotel was nowhere near ___ good as we'd expected.
fr: L'hôtel était loin d'être aussi bien que nous l'espérions.

explain.fr: nowhere near as… as = loin d'être aussi… que.
explain.en: nowhere near as… as.

say: The hotel was nowhere near as good as we'd expected.

question: She is by ___ the best candidate.
fr: C'est de loin la meilleure candidate.

explain.fr: by far + superlatif.
explain.en: by far + superlative.

say: She is by far the best candidate.

question: Prices are twice ___ high as last year.
fr: Les prix sont deux fois plus élevés que l'année dernière.

explain.fr: twice as + adjectif + as.
explain.en: twice as + adjective + as.

say: Prices are twice as high as last year.

question: She was elected ___ president of the association.
fr: Elle a été élue présidente de l'association.

explain.fr: Fonction unique après elect / appoint : pas d'article.
explain.en: Unique role after elect / appoint: no article.

say: She was elected president of the association.

question: ___ rich should pay more taxes.
fr: Les riches devraient payer plus d'impôts.

explain.fr: the + adjectif = groupe de personnes (the rich, the poor).
explain.en: the + adjective = group of people (the rich, the poor).

say: The rich should pay more taxes.

question: He was sent to ___ prison for fraud.
fr: Il a été envoyé en prison pour fraude.

explain.fr: Institution dans sa fonction : go to prison, to school, to church (sans article).
explain.en: Institution in its normal function: go to prison, school, church (no article).

say: He was sent to prison for fraud.

question: His mother went to ___ prison to visit him.
fr: Sa mère est allée à la prison pour lui rendre visite.

explain.fr: Le bâtiment (pas sa fonction) : the prison.
explain.en: The building (not its function): the prison.

say: His mother went to the prison to visit him.

question: She was oblivious ___ the danger.
fr: Elle était inconsciente du danger.

explain.fr: oblivious to / of.
explain.en: oblivious to.

say: She was oblivious to the danger.

question: The decision is subject ___ approval by the board.
fr: La décision est soumise à l'approbation du conseil.

explain.fr: subject to = soumis à.
explain.en: subject to.

say: The decision is subject to approval by the board.

question: He has a tendency ___ exaggerate.
fr: Il a tendance à exagérer.

explain.fr: tendency to + verbe.
explain.en: tendency to + verb.

say: He has a tendency to exaggerate.

question: They're on the verge ___ bankruptcy.
fr: Ils sont au bord de la faillite.

explain.fr: on the verge of.
explain.en: on the verge of.

say: They're on the verge of bankruptcy.

question: This is in keeping ___ our values.
fr: Cela correspond à nos valeurs.

explain.fr: in keeping with = conforme à.
explain.en: in keeping with.

say: This is in keeping with our values.

question: She takes pride ___ her work.
fr: Elle est fière de son travail.

explain.fr: take pride in.
explain.en: take pride in.

say: She takes pride in her work.

question: We have no objection ___ your proposal.
fr: Nous n'avons aucune objection à votre proposition.

explain.fr: objection to.
explain.en: objection to.

say: We have no objection to your proposal.

question: He was acquitted ___ all charges.
fr: Il a été acquitté de tous les chefs d'accusation.

explain.fr: acquit of.
explain.en: acquit of.

say: He was acquitted of all charges.

question: Hardly ___ the house when it started to rain.
fr: À peine étions-nous sortis qu'il s'est mis à pleuvoir.

explain.fr: Hardly + inversion au past perfect.
explain.en: Hardly + inversion with past perfect.

say: Hardly had we left the house when it started to rain.

question: I'd rather you ___ smoke in the car.
fr: Je préférerais que tu ne fumes pas dans la voiture.

explain.fr: I'd rather + autre sujet + prétérit.
explain.en: I'd rather + other subject + past.

say: I'd rather you didn't smoke in the car.

question: Suppose we ___ the train; what would we do?
fr: Imaginons que nous rations le train ; que ferions-nous ?

explain.fr: Suppose + prétérit (hypothèse).
explain.en: Suppose + past.

say: Suppose we missed the train; what would we do?

question: ___ you require further assistance, please contact us.
fr: Si vous avez besoin d'aide supplémentaire, contactez-nous.

explain.fr: Should + sujet = if (soutenu).
explain.en: Should = if (formal).

say: Should you require further assistance, please contact us.

question: But ___ your help, I would never have finished.
fr: Sans ton aide, je n'aurais jamais fini.

explain.fr: but for = sans (soutenu).
explain.en: but for = without.

say: But for your help, I would never have finished.

question: ___ to win the lottery, what would you do?
fr: Si tu gagnais au loto, que ferais-tu ?

explain.fr: Were + sujet + to + verbe = if + sujet + were to.
explain.en: Were + subject + to + verb.

say: Were you to win the lottery, what would you do?

question: If he had taken the job, he ___ rich now.
fr: S'il avait accepté le poste, il serait riche aujourd'hui.

explain.fr: Conditionnel mixte : passé → présent.
explain.en: Mixed conditional.

say: If he had taken the job, he would be rich now.

question: You ___ as well tell her the truth now.
fr: Autant lui dire la vérité maintenant.

explain.fr: may / might as well = autant.
explain.en: may / might as well.

say: You may as well tell her the truth now.

question: He ___ have left already; his coat is gone.
fr: Il est sans doute déjà parti ; son manteau n'est plus là.

explain.fr: Déduction sur le passé : must have.
explain.en: must have.

say: He must have left already; his coat is gone.

question: You ___ have told me earlier! Now it's too late.
fr: Tu aurais pu me le dire plus tôt ! Maintenant c'est trop tard.

explain.fr: Reproche : could have + participe.
explain.en: Reproach: could have.

say: You could have told me earlier! Now it's too late.

question: She denied ___ the documents.
fr: Elle a nié avoir vu les documents.

explain.fr: deny + having + participe.
explain.en: deny + having + participle.

say: She denied having seen the documents.

question: He urged us ___ calm.
fr: Il nous a exhortés à rester calmes.

explain.fr: urge someone to + verbe.
explain.en: urge someone to.

say: He urged us to remain calm.

question: They warned me ___ go out alone.
fr: Ils m'ont averti de ne pas sortir seul.

explain.fr: warn someone not to + verbe.
explain.en: warn someone not to.

say: They warned me not to go out alone.

question: The conference, ___ was held in Geneva, was a success.
fr: La conférence, qui s'est tenue à Genève, a été un succès.

explain.fr: Relative explicative : which.
explain.en: Non-defining: which.

say: The conference, which was held in Geneva, was a success.

question: There were fifty applicants, most of ___ were graduates.
fr: Il y avait cinquante candidats, dont la plupart étaient diplômés.

explain.fr: most of whom.
explain.en: most of whom.

say: There were fifty applicants, most of whom were graduates.

question: The ease with ___ she won surprised everyone.
fr: La facilité avec laquelle elle a gagné a surpris tout le monde.

explain.fr: Préposition + which.
explain.en: Preposition + which.

say: The ease with which she won surprised everyone.

question: Little ___ that his life was about to change.
fr: Il était loin de se douter que sa vie allait changer.

explain.fr: Little en tête : inversion.
explain.en: Little at the start: inversion.

say: Little did he realize that his life was about to change.

question: At no point ___ that she was unhappy.
fr: Elle n'a jamais mentionné qu'elle était malheureuse.

explain.fr: At no point en tête : inversion.
explain.en: At no point: inversion.

say: At no point did she mention that she was unhappy.

question: Only when the results came in ___ the scale of the problem.
fr: Ce n'est qu'à l'arrivée des résultats que nous avons compris l'ampleur du problème.

explain.fr: Only when… : inversion dans la principale.
explain.en: Only when…: inversion in the main clause.

say: Only when the results came in did we understand the scale of the problem.

question: What surprised me ___ his calmness.
fr: Ce qui m'a surpris, c'est son calme.

explain.fr: What + proposition + was…
explain.en: Pseudo-cleft: What… was…

say: What surprised me was his calmness.

question: ___ his age, he runs marathons.
fr: Malgré son âge, il court des marathons.

explain.fr: despite + nom.
explain.en: despite + noun.

say: Despite his age, he runs marathons.

question: The project was approved, ___ with some reservations.
fr: Le projet a été approuvé, quoique avec quelques réserves.

explain.fr: albeit + groupe sans verbe.
explain.en: albeit + phrase.

say: The project was approved, albeit with some reservations.

question: ___ he is talented, he lacks experience.
fr: Bien qu'il soit doué, il manque d'expérience.

explain.fr: While (concession) + proposition.
explain.en: While (concession) + clause.

say: While he is talented, he lacks experience.

question: Hardly ___ came to the meeting.
fr: Presque personne n'est venu à la réunion.

explain.fr: hardly + any- (sens négatif).
explain.en: hardly + any-.

say: Hardly anyone came to the meeting.

question: There's ___ point in waiting any longer.
fr: Ça ne sert à rien d'attendre plus longtemps.

explain.fr: no + nom.
explain.en: no + noun.

say: There's no point in waiting any longer.

question: Don't forget, ___?
fr: N'oublie pas, d'accord ?

explain.fr: Question tag : on reprend l'auxiliaire de la phrase avec la forme inverse (affirmatif → négatif, négatif → affirmatif) et le pronom sujet.
explain.en: Question tag: repeat the auxiliary with the opposite polarity and the subject pronoun.

question: Somebody has taken my pen, ___?
fr: Quelqu'un a pris mon stylo, hein ?

explain.fr: Question tag : on reprend l'auxiliaire de la phrase avec la forme inverse (affirmatif → négatif, négatif → affirmatif) et le pronom sujet.
explain.en: Question tag: repeat the auxiliary with the opposite polarity and the subject pronoun.

say: Somebody has taken my pen, haven't they?

question: I don't think he's right, ___?
fr: Je ne crois pas qu'il ait raison, si ?

explain.fr: Question tag : on reprend l'auxiliaire de la phrase avec la forme inverse (affirmatif → négatif, négatif → affirmatif) et le pronom sujet.
explain.en: Question tag: repeat the auxiliary with the opposite polarity and the subject pronoun.

say: I don't think he's right, is he?

question: Neither of them came, ___?
fr: Aucun des deux n'est venu, si ?

explain.fr: Question tag : on reprend l'auxiliaire de la phrase avec la forme inverse (affirmatif → négatif, négatif → affirmatif) et le pronom sujet.
explain.en: Question tag: repeat the auxiliary with the opposite polarity and the subject pronoun.

say: Neither of them came, did they?

question: You used to live here, ___?
fr: Tu habitais ici avant, non ?

explain.fr: Question tag : on reprend l'auxiliaire de la phrase avec la forme inverse (affirmatif → négatif, négatif → affirmatif) et le pronom sujet.
explain.en: Question tag: repeat the auxiliary with the opposite polarity and the subject pronoun.

say: You used to live here, didn't you?

question: He ought to apologize, ___?
fr: Il devrait s'excuser, non ?

explain.fr: Question tag : on reprend l'auxiliaire de la phrase avec la forme inverse (affirmatif → négatif, négatif → affirmatif) et le pronom sujet.
explain.en: Question tag: repeat the auxiliary with the opposite polarity and the subject pronoun.

say: He ought to apologize, shouldn't he?

question: Few people believed him, ___?
fr: Peu de gens l'ont cru, si ?

explain.fr: Question tag : on reprend l'auxiliaire de la phrase avec la forme inverse (affirmatif → négatif, négatif → affirmatif) et le pronom sujet.
explain.en: Question tag: repeat the auxiliary with the opposite polarity and the subject pronoun.

say: Few people believed him, did they?

question: We must leave now, ___?
fr: Nous devons partir maintenant, n'est-ce pas ?

explain.fr: Question tag : on reprend l'auxiliaire de la phrase avec la forme inverse (affirmatif → négatif, négatif → affirmatif) et le pronom sujet.
explain.en: Question tag: repeat the auxiliary with the opposite polarity and the subject pronoun.

say: We must leave now, mustn't we?

question: There's no point in ___ for the bus.
fr: (attendre le bus)

explain.fr: « there's no point in » est suivi de la forme en -ing. Ici, « to » / « in » est une préposition : elle est suivie de -ing.
explain.en: “there's no point in” is followed by -ing.

say: There's no point in waiting for the bus.

question: There's no point in ___ jobs.
fr: (changer de travail)

explain.fr: « there's no point in » est suivi de la forme en -ing. Ici, « to » / « in » est une préposition : elle est suivie de -ing.
explain.en: “there's no point in” is followed by -ing.

say: There's no point in changing jobs.

question: There's no point in ___ home every Sunday.
fr: (appeler la famille tous les dimanches)

explain.fr: « there's no point in » est suivi de la forme en -ing. Ici, « to » / « in » est une préposition : elle est suivie de -ing.
explain.en: “there's no point in” is followed by -ing.

say: There's no point in calling home every Sunday.

question: We ended up ___ for the bus.
fr: (attendre le bus)

explain.fr: « end up » est suivi de la forme en -ing.
explain.en: “end up” is followed by -ing.

say: We ended up waiting for the bus.

question: We ended up ___ to work.
fr: (aller au travail à pied)

explain.fr: « end up » est suivi de la forme en -ing.
explain.en: “end up” is followed by -ing.

say: We ended up walking to work.

question: We ended up ___ dinner for the family.
fr: (préparer le dîner pour la famille)

explain.fr: « end up » est suivi de la forme en -ing.
explain.en: “end up” is followed by -ing.

say: We ended up cooking dinner for the family.

question: We ended up ___ the bill.
fr: (payer l'addition)

explain.fr: « end up » est suivi de la forme en -ing.
explain.en: “end up” is followed by -ing.

say: We ended up paying the bill.

question: She objects to ___ late.
fr: (travailler tard)

explain.fr: « object to » est suivi de la forme en -ing. Ici, « to » / « in » est une préposition : elle est suivie de -ing.
explain.en: “object to” is followed by -ing.

question:
Most of the apps on our phones are free, yet their creators make billions. The reason is simple: we pay not with money but with our attention. Every minute spent scrolling generates data that can be sold to advertisers. To maximize this, designers use techniques borrowed from psychology, such as endless feeds, unpredictable rewards and red notification badges that create a sense of urgency. Critics argue that this business model deliberately exploits human weaknesses and may be contributing to rising levels of anxiety, particularly among young people. Some former tech employees have even become vocal advocates for "humane technology", calling for apps that respect users' time rather than compete for it.

answer: By selling data generated by users' attention

question:
We tend to assume that the more options we have, the happier we will be. However, psychologist Barry Schwartz has argued that an abundance of choice can actually make us less satisfied. In a well-known experiment, shoppers who were offered twenty-four kinds of jam were far less likely to buy any than those offered only six. Faced with too many possibilities, people may become paralyzed, fearing they will make the wrong decision. Even when they do choose, they are more likely to regret their choice, imagining that one of the alternatives might have been better. Schwartz suggests that learning to accept "good enough" rather than seeking the perfect option is the key to greater contentment.

What is the common assumption mentioned at the beginning?

explain.fr: Réponse : « More options make us happier. ». Relisez le passage du texte qui en parle.
explain.en: Answer: “More options make us happier.”.

In a well-known experiment, shoppers who were offered twenty-four kinds of jam were far less likely to buy any than those offered only six. Faced with too many possibilities, people may become paralyzed, fearing they will make the wrong decision. Even when they do choose, they are more likely to regret their choice, imagining that one of the alternatives might have been better. Schwartz suggests that learning to accept "good enough" rather than seeking the perfect option is the key to greater contentment.

question:
Rewilding is an approach to conservation that aims to restore natural processes rather than manage nature in detail. Instead of planting trees or controlling animal populations, rewilders reintroduce key species and then largely step back. One famous example is the return of wolves to Yellowstone National Park in 1995. By hunting deer, the wolves changed their behavior: the deer avoided certain valleys, allowing trees to grow back, which in turn stabilized riverbanks and attracted birds and beavers. Not everyone is enthusiastic, however. Farmers in several European countries fear for their livestock, and critics question whether ecosystems can ever truly return to a "natural" state after centuries of human influence.

What is the main idea of rewilding?

answer: Restoring natural processes and stepping back

question:
In many education systems, failure is seen as something to be avoided at all costs. Students are rewarded for correct answers and penalized for mistakes. Yet a growing body of research suggests that struggling with difficult problems, and sometimes failing, leads to deeper learning. When students attempt a problem before being taught how to solve it, they often get it wrong, but they later understand the underlying concepts better than those who were shown the method first. This phenomenon, sometimes called "productive failure", challenges the idea that teaching should always proceed smoothly from simple to complex. Its proponents argue that schools should create safe environments in which students feel free to take intellectual risks.

How is failure usually seen in education systems?
fr: Lisez le texte, puis répondez : Comment l'échec est-il habituellement perçu dans les systèmes éducatifs ?

explain.fr: Réponse : « As something to be avoided ». Relisez le passage du texte qui en parle.
explain.en: Answer: “As something to be avoided”.

question:
Scientists have long known that sleep is essential for health, but its role in memory has only recently become clear. During deep sleep, the brain appears to replay the experiences of the day, transferring information from short-term storage in the hippocampus to long-term storage in the cortex. Students who sleep after learning new material tend to remember it significantly better than those who stay awake. Conversely, pulling an all-nighter before an exam may be counterproductive: without sleep, the brain struggles both to retain new information and to retrieve what it already knows.

question:
The gig economy refers to a labor market in which short-term contracts and freelance work replace permanent jobs. Delivery riders, ride-hailing drivers and online freelancers are typical examples. Supporters praise the flexibility it offers: workers can choose when and how much they work. Detractors counter that this flexibility often comes at the expense of security, as gig workers typically lack sick pay, pensions and protection against sudden dismissal. Courts in several countries have recently ruled that some platform workers should be classified as employees rather than self-employed contractors, a decision that could reshape the industry.

question:
More than half of the world's population speaks at least two languages. Research suggests that being bilingual may offer cognitive advantages beyond communication. Bilingual people constantly manage two language systems, suppressing one while using the other, which may strengthen the brain's executive functions, such as attention and task-switching. Some studies have even found that lifelong bilingualism can delay the onset of dementia by several years.
